name: VWA Hardcore Saturday Night, 4 October 1997

date.source: The promotion's own two-part broadcast text, posted the same day.

matches.title: vwa-1998-north-american
matches.note: Predator won the North American Championship with a sudden rollup after Roger Rampage battered him outside the ring with a chair.

matches.title: vwa-1998-cruiserweight
matches.note: Quezzy reversed a Dirty Doug Foreyes top-rope move into a rollup to win the Cruiserweight Championship.
A non-title tag match; the Wyld Boyz won when Ace Diamond rolled up Psychotron after being distracted arguing with the referee.

matches.title: vwa-1998-world-heavyweight
matches.note: Alex Extreme won the World Heavyweight Championship from a Predator already worn down by his earlier title defense, finishing him with a moonsault into a legdrop billed as "The Extreme."

appearances.source: Announced at ringside accompanying Dirty Doug Foreyes for the Cruiserweight Championship match.

evidence.source: Part 1 of the promotion's own two-part broadcast text.
evidence.note: Opens with the North American and Cruiserweight title matches.

evidence.source: Part 2 of the promotion's own two-part broadcast text.
evidence.note: Carries the non-title tag match and the World Heavyweight Championship main event.

notes: The promotion's own broadcast team (commentators Jim Silvers and Matt Macklin, ring announcer Brett Butcher, and Ken Steeves reporting a Total War pay-per-view update) call the card but are not separately structured here.

name: VWA Hardcore Saturday Night, 13 December 1997

date.source: The promotion's own broadcast text, posted 16 December 1997 and dated in its own opening to 13 December.

matches.note: A non-title match; Frank White won in short order with a piledriver after Melcy Paradise missed a top-rope frog splash.
The champions Storm Inc. were awarded the match when the Brooklyn Brawlers, accompanied by the Slutty Slasher, walked away rather than face them a fourth time.
The main event; World Heavyweight Champion Nick Danger, accompanied by Roxy, defeated Ricky Davis with a Powerdriver.

appearances.source: Announced at ringside accompanying the Brooklyn Brawlers.
Announced at ringside accompanying Nick Danger and addressing Ricky Davis on his behalf.
Announced at ringside accompanying Ricky Davis.

evidence.note: A recap package opens the show naming King Suicide's own North American Championship, Storm Inc.'s own tag team reign, and Nick Danger's own World Heavyweight Championship (won "last month" at the promotion's own Hardcore Hell pay-per-view).

King Suicide and Robert Mulligan confront and beat down President Todd Bloom on-air, demanding a World Heavyweight Championship opportunity; Bloom books King Suicide against Predator and a further match for the promotion's own Christmas Clash pay-per-view.

notes: The promotion's own broadcast team (commentators Rex Rogers and Dan Crewman, ring announcer Brett Butcher, interviewer Ken Steeves) call the card but are not separately structured here. A planned Christmas Clash pay-per-view is announced on this broadcast but is not attested elsewhere in the held record.

name: VWA Hardcore Hell '97

date.source: The promotion's own 13 December 1997 broadcast recaps this pay-per-view as having taken place "last month"; the promotion's own November pay-per-view calendar names it "Hardcore Hell."

evidence.source: The promotion's own 13 December 1997 broadcast recap.
evidence.note: President Todd Bloom is shown presenting the World Heavyweight Championship to Nick Danger at this event; no other result survives.

notes: No card script for this pay-per-view survives in the held record; its existence and one result are known only from a later broadcast's own recap package.
